hyps.why: Adding a 3x3 conv on the direct input-to-output edge gains more when it replaces a missing edge than when it replaces an op that already carries signal.
Restoring the direct edge with a conv gives a larger gain than swapping one existing op for another.
Edge 0 feeds nodes 1 and 2 and then 3, so replacing none with a conv reconnects a lot of the cell.
Edge 5 is a final-hop edge into the output, so a conv replacing none helps more than a conv replacing another op.
Upgrading from a 1x1 conv to a 3x3 conv gives only a small gain compared with replacing a weak op.
A skip on the direct edge helps trainability and gives a gain when it fills an empty edge, but little when it replaces a conv.
A skip replacing none adds a path, while a skip replacing a conv loses capacity.
Removing a 3x3 conv costs more accuracy than removing a weak op such as pooling.
Deleting a strong direct conv edge hurts more than deleting a weak one.
Edge 2 connects the two intermediate nodes, so a conv replacing none adds depth and a path, which gives a larger gain than swapping ops.
